description: Handshake transcript construction, as specified in RFC-0001 section 5.4 and RFC-0002 section 5.1. The transcript is built from received bytes and hashed with SHA-256; the hash is then bound into the AUTH proofs. 'transcript_bytes' is the exact byte string that is hashed, so an implementation can be checked without a full session.

components.encoding: u16 big-endian length prefix, then UTF-8 bytes
u16 big-endian length prefix, then UTF-8 bytes

transcript_format.note: The two identifiers are length-prefixed so that a client_id ending in a byte sequence that looks like a separator cannot be confused with a different pair of identifiers. The four fixed-width 32-byte fields need no prefix. An implementation that mis-sizes any component here produces a transcript that agrees with itself and with no peer, which is why the arithmetic is recorded per vector and recomputed by the verifier.

vectors.note: Synthetic values chosen so a reader can verify the layout by hand: the nonces are 0x00-0x1f and 0x20-0x3f, the public keys are 0x40-0x5f and 0x60-0x7f.

expected.note_on_hash: transcript_sha256 is the SHA-256 of transcript_bytes, recomputed by the verifier and by both implementations. It is a cross-check on the byte string, not an independent input.

vectors.note: Shortest possible transcript: both identifiers are one byte, so both length prefixes are 0x0001. Total = 16 + 1 + (2+1) + 1 + (2+1) + 1 + 128 = 153 bytes.

expected.note_on_length: This is the floor of the format. An implementation that computes any other length here has mis-sized one of the three separators or one of the two length prefixes.

rejection_vectors.note: A naive concatenation without length prefixes would let client_id='c' with agent_id='a' collide with client_id='c\x00a' and an empty agent_id. The length prefixes prevent it, and this vector pins that an implementation reproducing the naive form fails.

expected.transcript_arithmetic: 16 + 1 + (2+3 for "c\x00a") + 1 + (2+0 for the empty agent_id) + 1 + 128 = 154. This is one byte longer than transcript.minimum-length (153), because the empty agent_id contributes its 2-byte prefix and no payload while the client_id carries one extra byte.
expected.note_on_differ: The transcripts must be byte-distinct from transcript.minimum-length even though both describe a one-character split. The length prefix is what makes them distinct: without it, client_id="c\x00a" with an empty agent_id would serialise identically to client_id="c" with agent_id="a".
